GRP-POL-001|Version6.0|Internal

## 15.Issue and remediation management

## 15.1 Definition and sources

An issue is a weakness in the design or operation of a control, or a gap between the current and required state. Issues are recorded centrally in the Group Issue Management System regardless of source, so the Group has a single complete view of known control weaknesses. Sources include self-identification, RCSA, control testing, incidents, internal audit, external audit, regulatory examination and third-party assessment.

15.2Rating andtimeframes

| RATING | CRITERIA | TARGET REMEDIATION | APPROVALTOEXTEND |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Controlfailure exposing theGroup toCritical residualrisk.a zero-appetitebreach,or regulatoryaction | 30 days | BoardRiskCommittee |
| High | Key control absentor ineffective for a High- ratedrisk | 90 days | Group ExecutiveRiskCommittee |
| Elevated | Control design gap or inconsistent operation for an Elevatedrisk | 180 days | DivisionalRiskCommittee |
| Moderate | Efficiencyordocumentationweaknesswith limited exposure | 270 days | Riskowner |
| Low | Minor observation;improvementopportunity | 365 days | Risk owner |

## 15.3 Mandatory issue attributes

* Adescription stating the weakness, not the desired solution.

* Root cause, determined through structured analysis rather than asserted.

* The risk or risks affected, referenced to the Group Risk Register.

¢ Rating, with rationale, and a single named accountable owner at Director level or above.

* Agreed actions, each with its own owner and date, plus interim mitigation until permanent remediation lands.

•Original target date,retained permanently and never overwrittenby an extension.

## 15.5 Extensions and overdue issues

Extension requests must be submitted before the due date, with the reason for slippage, revised date, interim mitigation and evidence that resourcing has been addressed. Retrospective extensions are not permitted. A second extension requires approval one level above the normal authority; a third requires Board Risk Committee approval regardless of rating.

## 15.6 Thematic analysis and closure

The Group Risk function performs quarterly thematic analysis across the issue population to identify common root causes, recurring designed appropriately, is operating, and has been tested at least once since implementation. For Critical and High issues, closure is failures, repeat findings and concentrations by system, process, third party or location.
